look_here_first: Colony-forming woodland sedge with broad leaves and several long drooping pistillate spikes below a raised cluster of staminate spikes.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Personal List in repaired Master Plant Pool; Texas-native under current Kew/GRIN.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; exact target-zone county reconciliation is deferred and native metrics remain excluded.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Cyperaceae/Carex: grasslike sedges with sheathing leaves; the fruit is enclosed in a perigynium, and perigynium shape/beak/venation are often decisive for species ID.
best_field_traits: leaf blades relatively broad, about 2.5–7 mm
proximal pistillate spikes arching or drooping
staminate spikes conspicuously raised above pistillate spikes
mesic forest, floodplain, streambank and calcareous woodland habitat
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Among these five, C. cherokeensis is the broad-leaved drooping-spike woodland sedge. It is much taller and looser than C. texensis and lacks the silvery winged perigynia of C. tetrastachya.
